local_helper_obligations.provides: For finitely many a_1..a_N in the open disk of radius Rfac: Q(z) = prod_v Rfac (z - a_v) / (Rfac^2 - conj(a_v) z) is analytic on the open disk, |Q| = 1 on |z| = Rfac, |Q(0)| <= 1, its zero set is exactly the a_v with multiplicity, and each factor obeys |factor(z)| >= |z - a_v| / (Rfac + |z|).
local_helper_obligations.why_local: REVISED round 3 per the correction: this is NOT an absent research-scale theory. Each factor is a complex RATIONAL function whose denominator is nonvanishing on the closed disk (|conj(a_v) z| < Rfac^2 for |a_v| < Rfac, |z| <= Rfac), so analyticity is `AnalyticAt.div` (Mathlib/Analysis/Analytic/Constructions.lean, confirmed) applied factorwise and `AnalyticOnNhd.prod` (same file, confirmed) over the finite index; the boundary identity |Q| = 1 on |z| = Rfac is the elementary algebraic identity |Rfac^2 - conj(a) z| = Rfac |z - a| for |z| = Rfac (expand both squared moduli; `Complex.normSq`/`Complex.mul_conj` algebra), the per-factor lower bound is the triangle inequality |Rfac^2 - conj(a) z| <= Rfac (Rfac + |z|), |Q(0)| <= 1 is |a_v|/Rfac <= 1 factorwise, and the zero/multiplicity clause is `AnalyticAt.order_mul` / `Finset.prod` of orders (already used by lem:l1-nuisance-zero-free). No Blaschke-space theory, no interpolation, no boundary-value theory is needed - only the finite product of explicit Mobius factors.

thm:known-zero-instrument.notes: Build-inline (medium). Four sub-claims: shift annihilation E_P[J(eta+d)] = 0 for every real d (binomial expansion + M^{(j)}(z0) = 0 for j < ell); the conditional version E_P[J(Z_n)|X] = 0 (ass:independent-treatment-noise, D_n is sigma(X)-measurable and bounded by 2Cg); E_P[Z_n J(Z_n)] = M^{(ell)}(z0) H_n(z0) (Leibniz on the factorization); and the ratio identity. REUSE (round-3 precision): the UNWEIGHTED steps reuse `ProbabilityTheory.complexMGF` and its analyticity/derivative API (Mathlib.Probability.Moments.ComplexMGF) - `iteratedDeriv_complexMGF` / `hasDerivAt_integral_pow_mul_exp` give exactly M^{(j)}(z) = E_P[eta^j e^{z eta}] and the differentiation-under-the-expectation step, the piece that would otherwise be hardest. The FINAL numerator E_P[Y J_{z0,ell}(Z_n)] is a WEIGHTED value (weight Y, exponent Z_n) and so is read off the S3 LOCAL weighted-transform layer - it is the (ell-1)-st derivative of `weightedTransform Y Z_n P` at z0 - not from complexMGF; its integrability is the note's own Cauchy-Schwarz/sub-Gaussian envelope, and the vanishing of the b_n(X) and xi contributions is the conditional-annihilation plus ass:outcome-mean-independence step. ROUND-5 CLOSURE (FLAG-wrong-decl): the transform factorization E_P[e^{z Z_n}] = M(z) H_n(z) that this proof differentiates ell times, and the weighted vanishing E_P[b_n(X) J(Z_n)] = 0, both route through the SAME ℂ-valued independent product-integral step as lem:observable-factorization, so this node uses `ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun.integral_fun_comp_mul_comp` (Mathlib/Probability/Independence/Integration.lean:206, `[RCLike 𝕜]` hence available at ℂ) and NOT the withdrawn `Causalean.Mathlib.IndepIntegral`; `Mathlib.Probability.Independence.Integration` is added to this node's modules accordingly, and the same measurability bridges recorded on lem:observable-factorization (AEMeasurable eta / X, AEStronglyMeasurable of each composed factor against the pushforward law, plus the separately supplied exponential-moment envelope, since the lemma itself assumes no integrability) apply verbatim here. Hypotheses are bundled: all three assumption dependencies (independent noise, outcome mean independence, eta sub-Gaussian) are fields of NonGaussianClass.

prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy.notes: Build-inline (small-medium) - fully in scope and independent of every Defer item.
